method: A separate local parser, without importing the collector, parsed every requests/size_bins/segment/cpu_endpoints row from all three preserved raw snapshots; independently recomputed every numeric delta, lifetime-max pair and per-call mean and compared the entire result to delta. Reviewed the measurement boundaries in the exact local driver and probe.

probe_coverage.interpretation: The aggregate has 5 more read requests and 266240 more read bytes than the probe minimum, plus 21 writes. This is consistent with background I/O and different measurement-window endpoints; aggregate counters cannot identify each request or prove that background reads did not mask a smaller omission. The probe itself performs no storage writes.

phase_accounting.interpretation: Read copy accounts for 51.0454568% of measured read-service wall time, and command_wait 48.2177882%. dma_start includes pre_reset and must not be added to it. The remaining 14.213 ms is time inside service but outside the listed measured subsegments, not an independently identified cause. command_wait includes command issue, MMIO polling, requested sleeps and intervening scheduling; it is not a direct controller-only or sleep-only timing.

interpretation_correction.finding: The raw generic statement different_means_at_least_one_migration is too broad for dispatch. dispatch begins in t736_request and ends in t736_worker, which are different execution contexts. Its 8197 differing endpoint pairs show submitter-to-worker CPU handoff, not 8197 migrations of one thread.
interpretation_correction.correction: Apply the at-least-one-migration interpretation only to measured segments executed within the same worker task. For dispatch, report different submitter/worker CPUs. No change to raw counters or measured data is needed.

limits: No board operation, runtime executable inspection, upload or new hardware test was performed by this reviewer. This review establishes local evidence consistency, not independent provenance of the running kernel.
Timing segments measure wall time including interrupts and scheduling; 4.724849806 seconds is read-copy segment wall time, not independently measured copy CPU time.

Same CPU endpoints do not establish residency. The CPU 5 versus CPU 6/7 per-call mean differences are observations with no controlled CPU frequency/load or per-CPU request-size attribution; they do not prove a cache or CPU-class cause.
Worker CPU time is tick-quantized and includes its work in the task-counter window; whole-system CPU includes all tasks. Neither can be equated directly to an individual phase.
Snapshot, syscall, worker-counter and diskstats windows differ. First-after stability over 18.893756 ms is not hardware draining or proof that no request was outstanding.
Only the first 8 MiB is repeated 64 times with O_DIRECT and a prefaulted destination. Device-internal cache may be warm; this is not unique-media streaming or content integrity validation.
Lifetime maxima remain before/after observations; their difference is not an interval maximum.
The measured cost justifies evaluating a cacheable payload-bounce experiment while retaining correctness checks; it does not prove that cacheability alone will recover a particular throughput.
